title: Clip a wafer onto an e-beam evaporator's sample plate and load it face down
instruction: Mount the wafer on the sample plate for e-beam evaporation, load it into the load lock once its light is green, then shut and lock the door. Tighten each clip screw 300 to 420 degrees; keep the door open under 2 minutes in all.
context: The evaporator coats from below, so the wafer hangs face down: it must be centred and held by clips that bite its round edge, enough of them, with screws that fit and are snug but not so tight they crack it. An open load lock takes on air and water that slow its pump-down and load the main chamber. Its light tower shows blue while a process runs (keep the door shut), green when it is done, orange for a warning and red for an error (tell the staff first). Loading wafers for metal deposition is a routine manual step in research cleanrooms that prototype new chips, including AI hardware. Closest accepted look-alike: TK-KFJZY8 holds a picture-frame back while rotating retaining clips. Here a fragile wafer is edge-clamped with threaded clips, inverted in a carrier and loaded through an interlocked door.
setup: Bench top as the origin's level; angles on the plate are measured from +x (towards the load lock), 90 degrees towards the left arm. Loading stand (painted steel, fixed) at (0.18, 0) m, its top 130 mm high, with a socket that takes the plate's boss. On it, face up: a stainless sample plate 200 mm across and 1.5 mm thick (0.36 kg) with rings of tapped holes for other wafer sizes, and eight steel swing clips (15 x 4 x 1 mm tabs, 13 mm from pivot to tip) in its 4 inch ring, 59.5 mm out, every 45 degrees, each on an M3 x 4 slotted cheese-head screw (ISO 1207, over a 0.5 mm shim washer; the simulation draws a 7 mm head with a 3.2 mm slot as a contact margin; a white paint mark on one side of the slot), parked along the rim with its screw backed off 0.35 mm. Only the tabs hold the wafer: a loose tab stands 0.35 mm over it, and tightening its screw presses it down onto the wafer's edge. The 225 degree clip's screw is too long (M3 x 12): its head stands 8 mm proud. On the plate: a 100 mm silicon wafer, pattern up, its primary flat facing the 90 degree clip, its centre 5 mm off the plate's centre towards 202.5 degrees. A steel screwdriver (0.8 x 5 mm blade, 5 mm square shaft 52 mm long, red 12 mm square handle 14 mm long, 35 g) stands blade down in a black block holder (30 x 30 x 60 mm, 6.5 mm square socket 12 mm deep, fixed) at (0.12, -0.17). Load lock (painted steel, fixed, glass viewport on top): a box 0.28 m deep (x = 0.36 to 0.64 m), 0.76 m wide and 350 mm tall. The load lock has just been vented. Its front opening, 0.75 m wide and 100 to 320 mm above the bench, is closed by an aluminium door (6 mm thick, 0.25 kg) that slides up 250 mm, with a 12 mm round handle bar 25 mm in front, 200 mm high when shut. It starts shut and locked by a black T-shaped twist lock on the door's front, right of the handle (its bar's centre at (0.336, -0.20), 150 mm up when shut): upright it holds the door on its seat; a quarter turn clockwise (seen from the robot) lays it level and frees the door. Lifted to the top, a latch holds the door open; pulled 25 mm down off the latch (about 8 N), it slides down under its own weight. On the load lock's top at (0.40, 0.30) stands a light tower (red, orange, green, blue, top to bottom); a lit lamp's bright lens stands out of its band. Blue is lit at the start, green from 8 s on. Inside, a steel holder on a centre shaft at (0.485, 0): two arcs 170 mm high between low fences. On it lies an aluminium ring holder (220 mm across, 180 mm inside, 4 mm thick, 0.14 kg) with a 1.5 mm recess under its rim that fits the plate.
scoring: Measured at the end, once both hands are released (all six jaw and pad points at least 80 mm from every task surface: the plate with its clips and screws, the wafer, the ring holder, the screwdriver, the door with its handle and lock, and the fixed apparatus) and every moving task part, the clips, screws, screwdriver, door and lock included, has moved under 1 mm in the last 1 s; 0 if not. 0 if, at any time, the long screw was turned over 90 degrees, a swung-in clip's screw was turned over 420 degrees (the wafer cracks), the door was lifted (over 3 mm off its seat) while the light was blue or was open more than 120 s in all, the wafer left its seat on the plate (centre over 8 mm off, or lifted), the plate or ring holder fell below 100 mm, or a fingertip came within 4 mm of the wafer's pattern (inside its 5 mm edge exclusion); 0 if the screwdriver is inside the load lock. Otherwise 0 unless the wafer is centred on the plate (within 2 mm) and held by clips that leave no gap over 150 degrees round it: a clip holds if it was swung in past 70 degrees, then its screw turned at least 300 degrees clockwise, its tab presses the wafer (in the simulation: the larger of its spring deflection and tab/wafer overlap is at least 0.03 mm, with spring deflection at least 0.005 mm; the overlap includes contact compliance and is not a measured clamp force), and its tip lies at least 2 mm inside the wafer's outline. 0.25 for that; 0.5 if also the ring holder lies face down on the load lock's holder (within 5 degrees, centre within 4 mm) carrying the plate face down (centred on it within 3 mm); 0.75 if also the door is shut (within 3 mm of its seat); 1.0 if also it is locked (its lever turned back within 10 degrees). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The untouched start scores 0. Real trial: use synchronized overhead and side video with a millimeter scale and screw-head paint marks to check the stated order, rotations, door timer and pattern exclusion; a ruler and square-on photos check wafer/plate offsets, clip overlap, carrier orientation, door seating and final hand clearance. Set each normal screw start with a 0.35 mm feeler gauge and qualify the actual clip stack before trials; nominal screw travel is not a measured clamp force. A tightened clip passes if a 0.03 mm feeler gauge cannot slide under its tip; the screw's turning torque is read with a 0.02 to 0.2 N m torque screwdriver during qualification.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; nothing is consumed. Clips start parked open; every M3 x 0.5 clip screw is backed off to 0.35 mm between its head and its tab (feeler gauge), so 300 to 420 degrees after swinging in makes it snug; the long M3 x 12 screw stands 8 mm proud. Wafer, ring holder and screwdriver go back to their start; the load lock starts vented, its door shut and locked, its light blue. Real-trial parts, cutting files (make_parts.py), assembly and reset: README, Real-trial hardware.
fidelity: Tabs have 0.8 mm drawn clearance; screws close a 0.9 mm collider gap in 252 deg, then 0.5 mm/turn. Press=max(spring deflection, wafer/tab overlap), gated at 5 um spring deflection; holding needs 30 um. This proxy includes contact compliance, not measured force. Estimated screw torque rises with it. Screw slots are enlarged. The 420 deg damage rule is a proxy. Door uses 0.25 kg effective load without counterweight inertia. No vacuum physics. Demo reads state.
